subject: Retention windows and deletion proof for logs, backups, and prompts — Veridian Health
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@veridianhealth.com>

Cc: Veridian Legal <legals@veridianhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Retention evidence request and DPA amendment ask

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the demo last week. As part of our security intake and DPA review we need some concrete evidence and timelines on Redwood's data retention and deletion practices so our compliance team can sign off. High level asks below, attached is Veridian's standard evidence request PDF for reference (veridian-evidence-request-20261118.pdf).

Please confirm the following for hosted Redwood API and for Dedicated deployments where behaviors differ:

- API request logs and structured audit events: default retention period, location, and deletion process.
- System logs and application logs captured for troubleshooting: retention and whether they are included in backups.
- Backups and snapshots: snapshot frequency, retention windows for warm and cold backups, and deletion confirmation process.
- Prompt retention and prompt caching: whether raw prompts or user inputs are persisted to disk or backups, retention windows, and guaranteed purge timelines.
- KV cache and ephemeral caches: TTL behavior and whether these caches are ever written to persistent backups.
- Proof of deletion: what artifacts you can provide as evidence (deletion event IDs, S3 object lifecycle records, audit log entries).
- Any variances for HIPAA customers or customers requesting longer retention windows.

If you can provide a short matrix plus any artifacts or SOC2 evidence pointers that would be ideal. We may request a follow-up technical call after we review.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Head of Privacy and Compliance
Veridian Health

Subject: Re: Retention evidence request and DPA amendment ask

Hi Elena and team,

Thanks for the request. Please find a concise technical summary below; I attached a more detailed matrix and screenshots (redwood-data-retention-matrix-20261119.pdf, s3-lifecycle-screenshot-20261119.png). If you need low-level audit logs, we can provide redacted event ids and bucket lifecycle records under NDA.

Summary for hosted API (default)
- API request logs (ingress metadata and per-request telemetry): default retention 30 days. Logs live in a centralized logging cluster with 30-day TTL. Deletion: TTL-driven deletion + manual purge; deletion events are recorded in our audit log system.
- System and application logs: retained 90 days by default, rotated to warm storage. Not included in customer-accessible backups.
- Backups and snapshots: monthly snapshots retained 90 days for warm snapshots. We maintain encrypted cold backups for platform recovery for up to 2 years for customers with contractually-required archival; otherwise default is 90 days.
- Prompt retention and prompt caching: by default we do not persist raw prompt text to long-term backups for hosted API. Short-lived prompt cache (in-memory and local NVMe) is ephemeral and expires within 24 hours; cache eviction events are not written to backups unless customer enables persistent logging.
- KV cache: server-side KV caches are in-memory with TTLs; eviction occurs per workload policy. KV contents are not included in standard backups.
- Proof of deletion: we can provide S3 lifecycle records, audit log entries with deletion event ids, and a signed statement of deletion. For hosted API we can include a deletion-event export covering the objects and timestamps.

Variations for Dedicated or Private deployments
- Dedicated: customers can select extended log retention (30 90 180 365 day options) and opt into longer snapshot archival. Extended retention is billed and added to contract.
- Private on-prem: retention and backups follow customer-managed policies; Redwood will provide guidance and an artifact template for proof of deletion.

HIPAA notes
- For customers with HIPAA addendum we recommend enabling our dedicated snapshot archival option and a 1-year cold backup retention to satisfy evidence requests. Access to backup keys and KMS is auditable.

Artifacts we can provide
- redwood-data-retention-matrix-20261119.pdf (attached)
- S3 lifecycle screenshot showing object expiration rules (s3-lifecycle-screenshot-20261119.png)
- Audit log export snippet with deletion event ids (available after an approved NDA)
- SOC2 controls mapping that references log retention controls (we can provide the SOC2 trust report redacted and via our compliance portal)

If you confirm which retention profile you require for Veridian we will produce deletion evidence for that profile. Happy to walk the team through the matrix.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Privacy Engineering, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Retention evidence request and DPA amendment ask

Karthik,

Thanks for the clear matrix. A couple of clarifications so our security team can close the thread quickly:

1) Prompt data: we need explicit assurance that raw prompt text and any PHI present in prompts are not included in backups or cold snapshots for hosted API customers unless the customer explicitly enables request logging. Can you confirm and provide a sample deletion event id or a sanitized audit snippet showing a prompt purge?

2) KV cache: please confirm expected maximum window before eviction under normal load, and whether any replication could cause copies to exist longer than TTL.

3) Deletion SLAs: for Veridian we would like a contractual guarantee for prompt purge within 24 hours and deletion-event evidence within 72 hours. Is that achievable for hosted API or do we need Dedicated?

We appreciate the attachments. Also note Veridian's legal prefers that any changes to retention be captured in an amendment to the DPA; can you share the DocuSign when ready.

Regards,
Elena

Date: 2026-11-21T16:04:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Retention windows and deletion proof for logs, backups, and prompts — Veridian Health

Hi Elena,

Following up to confirm what we can contractually commit to for Veridian:

- Prompt purge SLA: we can commit to purge of raw prompt cache contents within 24 hours of a verified deletion request for hosted API when request-logging is not enabled. If request-logging is enabled, prompt content may be present in logs and will follow the selected logging retention profile.
- Deletion evidence SLA: we can provide deletion-event artifacts (audit log ids and S3 lifecycle records) within 72 hours of the purge completion. We will include redacted event ids in the evidence package.
- KV cache behavior: typical in-memory TTL is 0 24 hours depending on workload; we will document the expected eviction window per route. Replication is asynchronous and does not extend retention beyond configured TTLs.
- Backups and snapshots: for Veridian we recommend Dedicated profile with 1 year cold archive if you require long-term recoverability as part of HIPAA controls. For hosted API default backups do not include prompt caches unless explicitly enabled.

I have created a DPA amendment that captures the above SLAs and a DocuSign link is available here for your legal team: https://www.docusign.com/signed/VER-2026-0442-dpa

If acceptable, Sofia will coordinate picking a date/time for a technical call next week to demo the deletion evidence export and walk through the artifacts.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Director, Customer Success Operations, Redwood Inference
